name: Colchicine
route_note: oral tablet or capsule; low daily doses for prophylaxis and cardiovascular prevention, short courses for gout flares
originator: traditional remedy (Colchicum autumnale); URL Pharma (Colcrys, US NDA)

discovery.by: Pierre-Joseph Pelletier and Joseph Bienaimé Caventou
discovery.note: Alkaloid isolated from autumn crocus (Colchicum autumnale), a plant used for gout since antiquity; pure colchicine was isolated by Geiger in 1833.

tagline: An ancient crocus alkaloid for gout that became a heart-protection drug
summary: Colchicine is a plant alkaloid that binds tubulin and dampens neutrophil-driven inflammation. Used for gout for centuries, it also treats familial Mediterranean fever and pericarditis, and in 2023 a low-dose tablet became the first anti-inflammatory approved to reduce cardiovascular events.
mechanism: Colchicine binds β-tubulin and prevents microtubule polymerisation. In neutrophils this impairs migration, adhesion, degranulation and phagocytosis of urate crystals.

Disrupted microtubules also limit assembly of the NLRP3 inflammasome, reducing production of interleukin-1β and downstream IL-6 and CRP. Its narrow therapeutic index means toxicity rises sharply with overdose or with drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein.
uses: Treatment and prophylaxis of gout flares
Reduction of myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularisation and cardiovascular death in atherosclerotic disease (0.5 mg, Lodoco)

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Pelletier and Caventou isolate the active principle of Colchicum.

history.title: Familial Mediterranean fever
history.detail: Colchicine is shown to prevent attacks of familial Mediterranean fever.

history.title: First US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Colcrys, the first approved single-ingredient colchicine; unapproved versions are removed in 2010.

history.title: ICAP trial
history.detail: ICAP shows colchicine halves recurrence of acute pericarditis (NEJM 2013).

history.title: COLCOT
history.detail: Low-dose colchicine reduces ischaemic cardiovascular events after recent myocardial infarction.

history.title: LoDoCo2
history.detail: In chronic coronary disease, colchicine 0.5 mg reduces cardiovascular events by 31%.

history.title: Lodoco approved
history.detail: FDA approves colchicine 0.5 mg (Lodoco) to reduce cardiovascular risk in June 2023.

history.title: CLEAR SYNERGY
history.detail: CLEAR SYNERGY finds no cardiovascular benefit of colchicine started early after myocardial infarction.

serious: fatal toxicity in overdose or with CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors
neuromuscular toxicity and rhabdomyolysis (especially with statins)

facts: Colchicine was used in the US for decades without FDA approval until Colcrys in 2009.
Lodoco (2023) was the first anti-inflammatory drug approved specifically to reduce cardiovascular events.
